explanation: The Almighty Creator who led Israel out of Egypt and gave them the law at Sinai.
The title used for Jesus Christ, God's Son, who was raised from the dead in this chapter.
Apostle to the Gentiles who traveled with Barnabas to preach the gospel.
A faithful companion of Paul and an early Christian leader known for his encouragement.
People outside the Jewish nation, to whom the apostles now turned with the message of salvation.
This good news about God's kingdom through Jesus Christ and his death and resurrection.
God's gift that grants forgiveness of sins and eternal life, available to all who believe in the Lord.
The gathering place where Jews assemble to read the Scriptures, where Paul delivered his first sermon in Antioch of Pisidia.
God's commandments given through Moses, which show humanity's need for a Savior.
Biblical writers foretold the coming of the Messiah and his sufferings before he entered into glory.
Jesus' death on the cross as an offering for the sins of the world according to God's plan.
God raised Jesus from the dead, confirming that he is the Lord's Son and the Savior.
Trust in Jesus' words and deeds as the basis for receiving salvation apart from the demands of the law.
